events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Upper Kuskokwim Valley. This
includes the cities of McGrath, Nikolai, And Takotna.

* WHEN...From Monday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...The Kuskokwim River is currently at bankfull. Soils
remain moist and excessive runoff may result in localized flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain is forecast to begin Monday afternoon. Rain should
continue through Wednesday morning with storm total rainfall
expected to be around 1 to 2 inches. Minor pooling/ponding of
water in low-lying and flood prone areas is possible with the
already saturated ground conditions beginning on Tuesday. Small
stream and creek flooding is possible as we expect very high
water levels throughout the week in response to the heavy rain.

- The Kuskokwim River at McGrath is at bankfull as of 12:00PM
AKDT Sunday September 13th. Water levels are forecast to drop
below bankfull by Monday morning. River levels are expected to
rise again in response to the heavy rain beginning Monday
afternoon and remain high through the rest of the week.

- We will continue to monitor the situation closely and update as
necessary.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc

Wash, Mineral Creek, Agua Fria River, Antelope Creek, Badger Spring
Wash, Chaparral Gulch, Wolf Creek, Grapevine Creek and Cedar Creek.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk: Water levels as
high as 1.0 to 2.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 40 to 45 mph before
winds transition to west Tuesday morning, diminishing impacts.

Toksook Bay and Tununak: West winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
45 to 50 mph beginning Tuesday morning. Water levels as high as
0.5 to 1.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kwigillingok,
Kongiganak, Kipnuk, Toksook Bay, and Tununak.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Monday to 10 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is potential for coastal erosion due to high
surf. The coastal flood threat is low to medium for
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk (30 to 40 percent). The
coastal flood threat is low (10 to 20 percent) for Toksook Bay
and Tununak.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A developing low pressure system will drive
a fetch of strong southwest winds towards the Kuskokwim Delta
Coast early Monday afternoon, which will result in increased
wave activity. Large breaking waves of 3 to 5 feet for the
Kuskokwim Delta coast will continue into Tuesday morning, which
will also coincide with high tide, enhancing coastal impacts.
Southwest winds shut off later Tuesday morning for the Kuskokwim
Delta Coast and attention then shifts to Toksook Bay and Tununak
as west winds take over and the low moves inland. Strong west
winds will bring in higher seas of 1 to 3 feet for Toksook Bay
and Tununak. Conditions are on track to improve as the low moves
farther inland Tuesday night. Additionally, periods of moderate
to heavy rainfall will precede the advisory duration.
